options.content:
**How to use this dashboard** — answer five questions in order; each row answers one.

1. **Is the server overloaded?** CPU, load, disk stall.
2. **Is it PostgreSQL?** The cluster's CPU against other process families.
3. **Queries or background work?** CPU by backend type: client queries, or autovacuum, checkpointer, I/O workers.
4. **Which query?** The digests with the largest share of the node's CPU or disk reads.
5. **Cause or victim?** Where query time goes: a query that mostly *waits* is a victim — fix the culprit, not the victim.

**Words used here.** *Digest*: one query shape — the SQL with its values replaced by `?`, so `id = 1` and `id = 2` count together. *Run-queue wait*: time a query was ready to run but no CPU was free. *WAL*: PostgreSQL's write-ahead log; a commit waits for it to reach disk. *Backend type*: what a PostgreSQL process does (client connection, autovacuum, checkpointer, I/O worker…). The full evidence for one moment is in `/api/diagnose` → `postgres_report.overload_cause`.
Red here means the machine itself is out of CPU or stuck on disk. If everything is green, slow queries have another cause (locks, the network, the client).

panels.title: Node CPU used
panels.description:
What: how busy all CPUs of the server were, averaged over 5 minutes.
Good / bad: below 70% is comfortable; above 85% queries start to wait for a CPU.
If bad: go to row 3 and 4 to see who uses the CPU.
Formula: avg_over_time(obs_agent_cpu_usage_percent[5m]).

panels.title: Load per CPU
panels.description:
What: processes running or waiting to run, per CPU (1-minute load average).
Good / bad: below 1 is fine; above 1.5 means work queues up for CPUs or disk.
If bad: if CPU is low but load is high, look at the disk stall panel.
Formula: obs_agent_load1 ÷ obs_agent_cpu_count.

panels.title: Disk stall (PSI io full)
panels.description:
What: share of time in which nothing on the server could progress because of disk I/O.
Good / bad: 0–2% is normal; above 10% the disk is stalling the machine.
If bad: open row 5 'Where query time goes' and the disk-read panels in row 4.
Formula: obs_agent_pressure_io_full_avg10 (kernel PSI, avg10). Absent on kernels without /proc/pressure.

panels.title: Tracing active
panels.description:
What: whether the agent's statement probes are attached (1) or not (0).
Good / bad: 1 is normal. 0 means the agent protected the database by detaching (statement rate too high) or could not load.
If bad: read postgres_report.accounting.state in /api/diagnose; the probes re-attach after postgres.shed_cooldown.
Formula: obs_agent_postgres_tracing_active.
Alert: ObsAgentPostgresTracingShed (warning) fires below 0.5 (== 0).

options.content: Compare the PostgreSQL cluster with the other process families. If another family is on top, the database is a victim of a neighbour.

panels.title: PostgreSQL cluster CPU vs top process families (cores)
panels.description:
What: CPU cores used by each PostgreSQL cluster and by the five busiest process families.
Good / bad: the cluster near the top while the node is busy means PostgreSQL is the main CPU user.
If bad: if another family is on top, look at process_report in /api/diagnose instead of the queries.
Formula: cluster: Σ rate(obs_agent_postgres_backend_cpu_seconds_total); family: obs_agent_family_cpu_percent / 100 × cpu_count.

options.content: Client queries are what applications send. Background work (autovacuum, checkpoints, I/O workers) is PostgreSQL maintaining itself; it has different fixes.

panels.title: CPU by backend type (% of cluster)

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (instance, cluster, backend_type) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_backend_cpu_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m])) / on (instance, cluster) group_left () sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_backend_cpu_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]))

panels.description:
What: each backend type's share of the cluster's CPU: client, autovacuum, checkpointer, io_worker, walsender…
Good / bad: client usually dominates; a background type above the dashed 50% line on a busy node is the cause.
If bad: autovacuum: check table bloat and autovacuum cost limits; checkpointer: raise max_wal_size; io_worker: queries are reading (row 4).
Formula: rate(backend_cpu_seconds_total) per type ÷ the cluster's total × 100, over 5m (the alert's window).
Alert: PostgresBackgroundCPUHigh (warning) fires above 50 (>= 0.5).

panels.title: Statement CPU coverage
panels.description:
What: how much of the cluster's CPU was spent inside statements the agent could see.
Good / bad: high (70–100%) means queries explain the load; low means background work or connection handling.
If bad: if low, read the backend-type panel on the left.
Formula: statement CPU ÷ cluster CPU × 100 (obs_agent_postgres_query_cpu_coverage_ratio).

panels.title: Disk reads by backend type (MB/s)
panels.description:
What: storage reads by each backend type of the cluster.
Good / bad: on PostgreSQL 18+ the io_worker line carries the reads of queries; autovacuum reading a lot means vacuuming big tables.
If bad: compare with row 4's disk-read shares; on PostgreSQL 18+ enable postgres.sql to split io_worker reads per query.
Formula: rate(obs_agent_postgres_backend_disk_read_bytes_total) / 1048576 (needs process.include_io).

options.content: A line above the dashed line is one query shape doing a fifth of all the server's CPU work or disk reads: that is the culprit to fix.

panels.title: % of node CPU used by top digests

targets.expr: 100 * topk(10, sum by (instance, cluster, digest_id) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_digest_cpu_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",digest_id!="other"}[5m])) / on (instance) group_left () (avg_over_time(obs_agent_cpu_usage_percent{instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) / 100 * obs_agent_cpu_count{instance=~"$instance"})) * on (instance, cluster, digest_id) group_left (digest_text) obs_agent_postgres_digest_info{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster"}

panels.description:
What: for the ten heaviest query shapes, their share of all CPU work on the server.
Good / bad: no line above the dashed 20% line is normal; one above it is a CPU culprit (the alert also needs the node ≥ 85% busy).
If bad: run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on it, add an index or cache, or slow its caller down.
Formula: rate(digest_cpu_seconds_total) ÷ node CPU cores in use × 100, over 5m.
Alert: PostgresDigestCPUHog (warning) fires above 20 (> 0.2).

panels.title: % of node disk reads by top digests

targets.expr: 100 * topk(10, sum by (instance, cluster, digest_id) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_digest_disk_read_bytes_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",digest_id!="other"}[5m])) / on (instance) group_left () (rate(obs_agent_node_disk_read_bytes_total{instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) > 0)) * on (instance, cluster, digest_id) group_left (digest_text) obs_agent_postgres_digest_info{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster"}

panels.description:
What: for the ten heaviest query shapes, their share of the disk's reads.
Good / bad: no line above 20% is normal; one above it reads a fifth of the disk (alert needs > 5 MiB/s). Empty on PostgreSQL 18+ async I/O.
If bad: 1–4 pages per call: add RAM / shared_buffers; hundreds: a scan — add an index or a LIMIT.
Formula: rate(digest_disk_read_bytes_total) ÷ rate(node_disk_read_bytes_total) × 100, over 5m.
Alert: PostgresDigestDiskReadHog (warning) fires above 20 (> 0.2).

panels.title: Top digests (last 5m)
panels.description:
What: the heaviest query shapes right now: CPU cores, share of node CPU, calls per second, disk reads.
Good / bad: a few cores spread over many digests is normal; one digest with a large share is the culprit.
If bad: copy its digest_id into the Analysis dashboard for history, or read its text in postgres_report.
Formula: per digest over 5m: rate(cpu seconds), ÷ node cores × 100, rate(calls), rate(disk read bytes) / 1048576.

options.content: A slow query that mostly waits for a CPU, the disk or the WAL is a victim of something else. Fix the culprit from row 4 first.

panels.title: Where query time goes

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_query_cpu_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",command="client"}[5m])) / sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_query_wall_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",command="client"}[5m]))

100 * sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_query_runq_wait_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",command="client"}[5m])) / sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_query_wall_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",command="client"}[5m]))

100 * (sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_query_io_wait_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",command="client"}[5m])) or 0 * sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_query_wall_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",command="client"}[5m]))) / sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_query_wall_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",command="client"}[5m])) + 100 * sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_query_wal_wait_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",command="client"}[5m])) / sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_query_wall_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",command="client"}[5m]))

panels.description:
What: of all time spent in client queries: running on a CPU, waiting for a CPU, and waiting for disk or the WAL.
Good / bad: waiting lines under the dashed 30% line are fine; above it queries are victims of a busy CPU or a slow disk.
If bad: CPU wait high: fix the CPU culprit (row 4) or add CPU. Disk + WAL high: check the disk and PostgresCommitsStalledOnWAL.
Formula: rate(part) ÷ rate(query_wall_seconds_total) × 100 for command=client, over 5m; an unmeasured wait counts as 0.
Alert: PostgresQueriesStarvedForCPU (critical) fires above 30 (> 0.3).
Alert: PostgresQueriesStalledOnDisk (critical) fires above 30 (> 0.3).

panels.title: WAL wait share

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_query_wal_wait_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",command="client"}[5m])) / sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_query_wall_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",command="client"}[5m]))

panels.description:
What: share of client-query time spent waiting for the write-ahead log to reach disk (mostly COMMIT).
Good / bad: a few percent is normal; above the dashed 20% line commits are slow.
If bad: check the WAL disk's latency; consider group commit (commit_delay) or synchronous_commit=off where safe.
Formula: rate(query_wal_wait_seconds_total) ÷ rate(query_wall_seconds_total) × 100, command=client, over 5m.
Alert: PostgresCommitsStalledOnWAL (warning) fires above 20 (> 0.2).

panels.title: Sync-replication wait share

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_query_syncrep_wait_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",command="client"}[5m])) / sum by (instance, cluster) (rate(obs_agent_postgres_query_wall_seconds_total{instance=~"$instance",cluster=~"$cluster",command="client"}[5m]))

panels.description:
What: share of client-query time spent waiting for synchronous standbys to confirm.
Good / bad: empty when synchronous replication is not used; above the dashed 20% line a standby is slow.
If bad: check pg_stat_replication lag, the standby's disk and network.
Formula: rate(query_syncrep_wait_seconds_total) ÷ rate(query_wall_seconds_total) × 100, command=client, over 5m.
Alert: PostgresSyncReplicationSlow (warning) fires above 20 (> 0.2).

panels.title: Statements per second by command
panels.description:
What: executed statements per second: client queries, fastpath calls, autovacuum and replication commands.
Good / bad: compare with yesterday: a jump in client statements often explains a CPU rise.
If bad: find the caller of the digest that grew in row 4.
Formula: rate(obs_agent_postgres_queries_total) by command.

options.content: Whether the numbers above are complete. Missing signals are shown as unavailable, never as zero.

panels.title: Accounting availability
panels.description:
What: which optional signals are measured (1) or not (0).
Good / bad: disk wait 0 usually means kernel delay accounting is off; enrichment 0 means postgres.sql is not configured or failing.
If bad: enable delay accounting (postgres.enable_delayacct) or fix the DSN; see accounting in /api/diagnose.
Formula: io_wait_available, wal_wait_available, enrichment_up gauges.

panels.title: Dropped, overflow, mismatches, unmatched credit
panels.description:
What: rates of the agent's own accounting problems.
Good / bad: all flat at zero is healthy; dropped above zero means totals undercount.
If bad: check the agent's CPU limit and the number of distinct statements.
Formula: rate() of the four obs_agent_postgres_*_total health counters.
